xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3216: Briefing reports "Troubled agents: 60" when the troubled gate holds 1 — it counts routine tmux reconciliation as distress

plan.title: Briefing "Troubled agents" line must count the troubled gate, not accumulated failure history
plan.author: agent:k3[1m]

narratives.Problem: The briefing fleet-health line labelled 'Troubled agents' filters on `agent.troubled || (agent.consecutiveFailures ?? 0) > 0` (src/lib/briefing-assembler.ts:151), so it counts every agent that ever recorded a consecutive failure — including 57 routine `orphaned: tmux session missing (reconcile)` records on stopped agents — as distress. The gate held 1 agent while the line reported 60. 'Troubled' is a precise gate (quarantines auto-resume, cleared by `pan untroubled`); the inflated number invites investigation of a non-problem and teaches readers to discount the whole briefing panel.
narratives.Proposal: Count what the label says (the issue's recommended option 1): narrow the filter at src/lib/briefing-assembler.ts:151 to `agent.troubled === true`. Add a regression test at tests/unit/lib/briefing-assembler.test.ts that builds a minimal DashboardSnapshot (1 troubled + 3 failure-only agents) and asserts the rendered line is `- Troubled agents: 1`, plus a zero case. The snapshot path of assembleLiveBriefingMarkdown is pure (no fs access), so no mocking is needed. No second 'recorded failures' line is added — per-agent failure displays already surface consecutiveFailures where actionable. Other broad-set consumers (feedback-target.ts:182, spawn.ts:170, lifecycle-stop.ts:347, untroubled.ts:26) intentionally keep the broad set because they clear/quarantine failure state. Do NOT filter by agent status: the troubled gate applies to stopped agents (the 1 gated agent at filing time was stopped).
narratives.NonGoals:
- Renaming the 'Troubled agents' label or adding a second 'agents with recorded failures' line
- Changing any other surface that consumes consecutiveFailures (frontend warning highlights, health endpoints, gate/untroubled logic)
- Cleaning up stale consecutiveFailures rows in the agents table
- Changing the other four fleet-health lines (Running agents, Active issues, Paused gates, Failed verification/review)
- Bootstrapping .pan/context/codebase/ (absent at planning time; out of proportion for a one-line fix)

autoDecisions.summary: Chose issue option 1 (filter on agent.troubled alone) over option 2 (broader filter + renamed/extra line)
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue names option 1 as recommended; 'troubled' already has a precise gate meaning elsewhere (resume quarantine, pan untroubled), and 57/60 of the broader population is routine reconciliation noise with no operator action attached.

items.title: Filter the briefing 'Troubled agents' line on the troubled gate alone and pin it with a regression test

expected_outputs: tests/unit/lib/briefing-assembler.test.ts exits 0, with a case asserting a snapshot of 1 troubled + 3 failure-only agents renders '- Troubled agents: 1'

narrative.Action: PRD: .pan/drafts/PAN-3216.md (promoted to drafts/pan-3216.md on overdeck-state at finalize). Step 1 — write tests/unit/lib/briefing-assembler.test.ts FIRST. Import { assembleLiveBriefingMarkdown } from '../../../src/lib/briefing-assembler.js' and type { DashboardSnapshot } from '@overdeck/contracts'. Build a minimal snapshot: { sequence: 1, agents: [...], specialists: [], reviewStatuses: [], issues: [], timestamp: new Date().toISOString() } as DashboardSnapshot; each agent needs at minimum { id, issueId, status } (AgentStatus literals: 'starting'|'running'|'stopped'|'error'|'unknown'). Case 1: 1 agent { troubled: true, status: 'stopped' } + 3 agents { consecutiveFailures: 1..3, status: 'stopped', troubled unset } → expect output toContain('- Troubled agents: 1'). Case 2: no troubled agents, several with consecutiveFailures > 0 → expect '- Troubled agents: 0'. The snapshot path does no filesystem access — no mocking needed. Run it and watch case 1 fail (renders 4). Step 2 — change src/lib/briefing-assembler.ts:151 from `snapshot.agents.filter((agent) => agent.troubled || (agent.consecutiveFailures ?? 0) > 0)` to `snapshot.agents.filter((agent) => agent.troubled === true)`. Nothing else changes: keep the variable name, the render line at :165, and the other four fleet-health lines. Do NOT add a status filter (the troubled gate applies to stopped agents). Do NOT touch other broad-set consumers (feedback-target.ts:182, spawn.ts:170, lifecycle-stop.ts:347, untroubled.ts:26). Step 3 — re-run the test; green. Then run the existing briefing suites and typecheck.

items.title: Given a snapshot with 1 troubled agent and 3 agents with consecutiveFailures>0 but no troubled flag, when assembleLiveBriefingMarkdown({ snapshot }) runs, then the output contains exactly '- Troubled agents: 1'
Given a snapshot with zero troubled agents and several failure-only agents, when the briefing is assembled, then the output contains '- Troubled agents: 0'

grep of src/lib/briefing-assembler.ts shows the troubledAgents filter expression no longer references consecutiveFailures, and the other four fleet-health lines (Running agents, Active issues with agents, Paused gates, Failed verification/review states) are unchanged
npx vitest run tests/cli/commands/briefing.test.ts tests/lib/briefing-freshness.test.ts exits 0 unchanged and npm run typecheck completes without errors
